title: Dependency Neighborhoods and Release Gateways: a structured approach to cross-team roadmap handoffs
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Roadmap-level dependencies across Engineering, Design, Security and Infra are tracked inconsistently (ad-hoc comments, email threads, brittle spreadsheets). This causes late discoveries of blockers during cutover, unclear ownership, and repeated rework across releases.

Goal: Deliver a lightweight but enforceable framework to model 'Dependency Neighborhoods' (logical groups of work that share a shipment horizon) and 'Release Gateways' (observable handoff gates with owners and acceptance criteria). The goal is to reduce last-mile blocked work by 40% for Q2 releases and improve cross-team SLA for signoffs from 65% to 90%.

Approach and deliverables:
- Define taxonomy and data model for a Dependency Neighborhood (fields: neighborhood id, owners by role, linked tickets, risk tier, expected cutover window).
- Implement gating checklist templates for Release Gateways: API contract freeze, infra capacity signoff, security review, design QA, canary rollback window.
- Build a minimal Linear-to-dashboard pipeline (backfill script + incremental sync) and a public-facing dashboard in Console that shows neighborhood status, required signoffs, and blocking tickets.
- Automations: auto-assign owners based on ownership matrix, notify slack channels when a neighborhood misses a gateway SLA, and create escalation path to on-call leads.
- Runbook & playbook: one-pager runbook for PM/Eng/Design leads with decision map and cutover checklist.

Success criteria (by due_date):
- Dashboard displays neighborhoods for 3 pilot initiatives and updates automatically from linked tickets.
- Blocked work observed in weekly roadmap review drops by >=40% for pilots.
- 90% on-time signoffs for gateway items across pilot neighborhoods.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Overhead: too many neighborhoods will increase process friction — will start with strict guardrails for pilot only.
- Data quality: relies on teams tagging tickets properly; mitigation: default auto-tagging heuristics and owner reminder nudges.
- Scope creep: avoid turning this into heavy governance; emphasize tooling+visibility first.

Stakeholders & collaborators:
- Eng (Platform): Omar Ben (eng lead), ENG-4120 owner: Priya Shah
- Design: Lina Park (lead designer), DES-231 (design tasks)
- Security: Devon Li (security reviewer)
- Infra/SRE: Marco Ruiz (infra coordination)
- PMs: Asha Kapoor (initiative owner), product partners for pilot: Rachel Moore, Luis Ortega

Acceptance criteria:
- Data model and checklist documented in Confluence and linked from this ticket.
- Dashboard prototype live and linked.
- Automation rules (owner assignment, slack alerting) deployed to staging and validated with 2 neighborhoods.

Notes on scope: the initial pilot will be limited to three neighborhoods (Console release features, Dedicated capacity rollout, and Private deployment security hardening). After measuring pilot metrics for one cycle, we will iterate and expand to additional initiatives.
